description: Artery is a vehicle-to-everything simulation framework maintained in the riebl repository. It implements ETSI ITS-G5 communication through GeoNetworking, BTP and a middleware that equips each vehicle with multiple services. It began as a Veins extension but now supports independent use. Users provide road scenarios, traffic demand and communication settings; SUMO supplies vehicle movement and OMNeT++ handles network events. Outputs describe the resulting service and communication behaviour. Coverage is global and scenario-defined, with no common observation period or fixed network size. Public C++ source is free under GPL-2.0, with installation and example instructions on the project website. OMNeT++ retains its separate licence conditions. A limitation is documentation age: the installation page was last updated in August 2023 and recommends OMNeT++ 5.6 while warning about the 6.x transition. Linux is the documented build platform, and compatible external submodules are required. Artery supports coupled road and communication experiments around SUMO (model-sumo) and OMNeT++ (platform-omnet-plus-plus). This review did not establish compatibility with their newest releases.
